chunks: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini said: He narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah [who said: Ahmad] ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari narrated from Sa'd ibn Dawud, from Abu Dahr, from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Nafi', who said:

I was writing a Quran codex for Hafsa, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), and she said: When you reach this verse, write: 'Maintain the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the identity of the middle prayer (Salat al-Wusta) according to Hafsa's dictation of the Quran?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the early exegetical tradition linking the 'middle prayer' (al-salat al-wusta) of Quran 2:238 specifically to Asr, a view supported by the practice of Hafsa bint al-Walid. It underscores the significance of preserving the distinct status of the afternoon prayer within the daily ritual structure, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the precise timing and reverence of the five daily prayers as established by the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by Ali bin Abdullah al-Warraq, and Ali bin Muhammed bin Hasan al-Qazwini, that they both said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Abi Khalaf al-Ash’ari, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Dawud, from Abu Dahr, from Malik bin Anas, from Zaid bin Aslam, from Amru bin Nafe’, that he said:

I was writing the book (which contained the Qur’an) from Hafsa, the wife of the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and she said: If you reach this verse, then write: «Maintain the prayers, and (in particular) the middle prayer and the prayer of the afternoon». [2:238]
